offences.quote: Submitting GenAI generated content without citation of the AI tool or evidence of how you used it (Principles 1 and 2)
Submitting GenAI generated content as if it were your own work (Principles 1 and 2)
"Using AI may not be cheating - but hiding it could be a breach of academic integrity."
Conversely, it is inappropriate to make any use of GenAI that creates an unfair academic advantage or passes off the work of others as if it were your own.
Paraphrasing text (whether published or the work of another student) in order to pass off the work of others as your own (Principles 1 and 2)
Fabricating empirical data to use in a research project or other assessment (Principles 2 and 3)
Uploading participant data or responses into GenAI without the participants' consent or ethical approval (Principle 6)

liability.quote: Whether malicious or accidental, use of any technology that breaches Academic Integrity can result in you being investigated for academic misconduct.

detection.quote: I have saved copies of GenAI outputs used in preparing my assessment. I know I may be asked to provide these as an appendix to my assessment or as part of any misconduct process.

process.quote: Whether malicious or accidental, use of any technology that breaches Academic Integrity can result in you being investigated for academic misconduct.
